name: Monitor portfolio credit risk (monthly risk report)
summary: Every month the risk and portfolio team turns the month-end data on about 55,000 contracts into a portfolio risk report. Analysts check the data load, reconcile balances to the ledger, collect restructure and recovery lists from operations, calculate delinquency, roll rates and losses, update vintage curves, concentrations, partner performance, the watch list and scorecard monitoring, and draft commentary that the director and the chief credit and risk officer review. The report feeds the loss allowance, lender reporting, planning, partner reviews, credit policy and the board. It is slow because data arrive from several systems and emailed spreadsheets, most analysis is done in spreadsheets that need checking, and reviewers ask for follow-up cuts.

baseline.org_archetype: A mid-size independent Canadian equipment lessor with a seven-person risk and portfolio team, a data warehouse fed nightly from the lease system and spreadsheet-based reporting.
baseline.notes: No prudential regulator; the report serves management, the board, auditors and funders. 2020 added deferral and restructure tracking.

trigger: Month end: the lease system's month-end batch completes and the snapshot loads into the data warehouse.
end_state: The approved report is distributed, extracts are sent to accounting, treasury, planning and the channels, and it has been presented at the credit and risk committee (and condensed for the board at quarter end).

volume.seasonality: Quarter-end months add board pages; year-end adds audit questions on the allowance. In 2020 deferral tracking and ad hoc requests roughly doubled the work for several months.

evidence.note: One report a month, as in the organisation file.
The analyses and reports are documented in supervisory guidance. FTE (about 0.8 of 4 analysts) is the author's estimate: modelled steps plus ad hoc follow-up questions the report generates.
Review, escalation and committee presentation. Author estimate.
Monthly sign-off. Author estimate.
Month-end load checks and fixes. Author estimate.

systems.name: Data warehouse and business intelligence reports
Lease management system (contracts, schedules, billing, tax codes, asset records, servicing)
Spreadsheet models (pool cuts, borrowing base, covenants, budget, tax workpapers)
Rule-based credit scoring and decision engine
General ledger and accounts payable (mid-market ERP)

steps.name: Load the month-end portfolio snapshot
steps.description: After the lease system's month-end batch, the nightly warehouse load writes the month-end snapshot: contract balances, days past due, payment deferrals and restructures, charge-offs, recoveries, and the channel, dealer, broker, industry, equipment and province of each contract.

evidence.note: Nightly warehouse loads are described in the organisation file; timing after month end is an author estimate.

steps.name: Check the load and control totals
steps.description: A data developer compares row counts and total balances in the warehouse snapshot with the lease system's month-end control report, checks that every scheduled job finished and looks for contracts with missing codes such as industry or channel.

error.defect_description: A partial load goes unnoticed, so some payments or charge-offs are missing.

control.basis: Data management standard: month-end loads are checked against lease system control totals before reports are released

evidence.note: Data integrity problems such as wrong industry codes and unreported delinquency are documented; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Re-run failed loads and fix mappings
steps.description: The data developer re-runs failed jobs, corrects code mappings (for example a new dealer without a channel code or a restructure flag that did not carry over) and reloads the affected tables.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Refresh scheduled risk reports and extracts
steps.description: The business intelligence tool refreshes the standard risk reports: delinquency buckets by count and balance, roll rates between buckets, charge-offs and recoveries, and extracts that feed the analysts' spreadsheets.

evidence.note: Automated reporting platforms for monthly portfolio monitoring are documented; timing is an author estimate.

steps.name: Reconcile portfolio balances to the ledger
steps.description: A portfolio analyst ties the warehouse's net investment, charge-offs and recoveries to the lease subledger and the general ledger figures from accounting, by product and funding pool, and lists differences above the tolerance.

control.basis: Reconciliation of portfolio risk data to the ledger, relied on by the external auditor for the loss allowance and by lenders for the borrowing base

evidence.note: Accurate MIS and loan review of data are documented; the wait for accounting's subledger figures and the times are author estimates.

steps.name: Investigate reconciliation differences
steps.description: The analyst traces differences contract by contract: timing of late payments, charge-offs booked in the ledger but not yet in the lease system, pools sold mid-month or contracts with wrong product codes, and agrees corrections with accounting or the data team.

next.condition: needs a data fix and reload

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Collect collections, restructure and recovery inputs
steps.description: The analyst asks the collections supervisors for the watch list and repossession pipeline, lease administration for deferrals and restructures not yet flagged in the system, and recoveries for write-offs, insolvencies and recoveries, which arrive as emailed spreadsheets.

error.defect_description: A team sends last month's file or leaves out some restructures.

evidence.note: Deferrals and restructures became a major portfolio feature in 2020; the hand-offs and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Calculate delinquency, roll rates and net losses
steps.description: In the report workbook the analyst calculates 31, 61 and 91-plus day delinquency by count and balance, roll rates between buckets, net charge-offs as an annualised share of average receivables, deferral and restructure balances, and splits them by channel, product, province, industry and equipment type against prior months and limits.

error.defect_description: Formula or bucket error in the workbook.

evidence.note: Delinquency, charge-off and nonperforming reports and the industry's over-30-day and net loss measures are documented; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Send the delinquency and loss extract to lease accounting
steps.description: The analyst sends lease accounting the delinquency buckets, roll rates, restructure flags and write-offs it needs for the expected credit loss allowance, with notes on unusual movements.

error.defect_description: Extract sent before late corrections, so the allowance uses stale figures.

control.basis: IFRS 9 impairment applied to lease receivables under IFRS 16: the expected credit loss allowance uses current delinquency, restructure and loss data that the auditor tests

evidence.note: IFRS 9 impairment applies to lease receivables; the hand-off timing is an author estimate.

steps.name: Update vintage and static pool curves
steps.description: The analyst adds the month to the cumulative loss and delinquency curves by origination quarter, compares recent vintages with older ones and with pricing and conduit assumptions, and adjusts loss rates for portfolio growth with lagged ratios.

error.defect_description: Cohort definition or denominator error in the vintage tables.

evidence.note: Vintage and lagged analysis and monthly pool performance disclosure are documented; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Analyse concentrations against policy limits
steps.description: The analyst measures exposure by industry, equipment type, province, dealer and broker and the twenty largest customer groups, compares each with the credit policy limits and flags breaches and near-breaches.

error.defect_description: Related customers not grouped, so a single-name exposure is understated.

control.basis: Board-approved credit policy limits on concentrations by industry, equipment type, region, originator and single obligor

evidence.note: Concentration reports and limits are documented; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Review dealer and broker performance
steps.description: The analyst ranks dealers and brokers by early defaults, first-payment defaults, fraud flags and delinquency on their recent bookings and lists partners above the thresholds for the vendor and broker channel reviews.

evidence.note: Tracking new loans by acquisition source is documented; partner thresholds and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Update the watch list and large-exposure summary
steps.description: The analyst adds and removes watch-list accounts using collections notes, restructures and the latest annual reviews of large exposures, records risk rating changes and summarises the largest troubled exposures and the expected loss on each.

error.defect_description: A deteriorating large exposure is not added to the watch list.

evidence.note: Problem loan and watch list reports and risk rating reports are documented; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Monitor scorecard and decision engine performance
steps.description: The analyst checks approval rates, overrides, the score mix of new applications and early bad rates by score band against the scorecard's expected values and notes drift for the credit policy manager.

evidence.note: Exception reports and monitoring of underwriting exceptions are documented; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Compare with industry indices and prior periods
steps.description: The analyst compares the company's delinquency and loss rates with the CFLA and PayNet Canadian equipment delinquency indices and the ELFA monthly index, and with the same month last year, to separate market-wide movements from company-specific ones.

evidence.note: Published Canadian and US delinquency and loss indices are documented; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Draft the report and commentary
steps.description: The analyst pastes the tables and charts into the report template and writes commentary on trends, drivers, breaches, the outlook and recommended actions, with a one-page summary for leadership.

error.defect_description: A figure is pasted from an old version or the commentary does not match the tables.

evidence.note: Reports must be analytical with history and trends, not only numbers; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Peer check the figures
steps.description: A second portfolio analyst ticks the main figures back to the extracts, checks formulas and links in the workbook and reads the commentary against the tables.

control.basis: Four-eyes check of report figures before management review

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Director reviews the draft
steps.description: The director of risk and portfolio management reads the draft, challenges the explanations for movements, asks for drill-downs on segments that worsened and edits the summary.

control.basis: Risk management policy: the director of risk reviews the monthly portfolio report before it goes to the chief credit and risk officer

evidence.note: Senior review of portfolio reports and a credit measurement and monitoring process are documented; shares and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Run follow-up analysis and revise
steps.description: The analyst runs the requested cuts, for example a vintage split by dealer or the deferral accounts' payment behaviour, updates the tables and commentary and sends the revision back.

error.defect_description: A new cut introduces an inconsistency with the main tables.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Chief credit and risk officer signs off
steps.description: The chief credit and risk officer reads the summary and breach list, adds the management view for the committee and approves distribution, or asks for more analysis.

control.basis: Board-approved risk appetite statement: the chief credit and risk officer signs off the monthly portfolio report and owns breach escalation

next.condition: approved with breaches or adverse trends to escalate

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Escalate limit breaches and recommend actions
steps.description: For concentration breaches, partners above thresholds or worsening vintages, the director writes recommended actions such as tighter cut-offs, a lower limit for an industry or restricting a dealer, and names the owner and date.

control.basis: Risk appetite statement: limit and trigger breaches go to the credit and risk committee with an action plan

evidence.note: Dashboards against risk appetite and action on concerns are documented; shares and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Distribute the report and extracts
steps.description: The analyst issues the report to leadership and the credit and risk committee and sends extracts to treasury for the borrowing base and covenants, planning, the vendor and broker channel managers, the mid-ticket credit team and the enterprise risk analyst.

evidence.note: Recipients follow the organisation file's process map; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Present at the monthly credit and risk committee
steps.description: At the monthly credit and risk committee the director walks through the summary, breaches and actions; decisions and new requests are minuted and assigned.

control.basis: Credit and risk committee terms of reference: monthly portfolio review

evidence.note: Clear and timely portfolio information to senior management and the board is expected; the committee cadence is an author estimate.

steps.name: Prepare the board risk committee pages
steps.description: At quarter end the director condenses three months of results into the board risk committee pages: risk appetite measures against limits, trends, breaches and actions, in the summary form boards expect.

control.basis: Board risk committee charter: quarterly portfolio risk report from management

next.condition: pages delivered to the board secretary

evidence.note: Board reports should be summarised and readily understandable on risk levels and trends; times are author estimates.

exceptions.name: Failed or partial month-end load
exceptions.description: A warehouse job fails or codes are missing, so the data developer reloads before analysis can start.

exceptions.name: Balances do not reconcile to the ledger
exceptions.description: Differences with the subledger or ledger have to be traced contract by contract, sometimes needing a data fix.

exceptions.name: Reviewer asks for follow-up analysis
exceptions.description: The director or the chief credit and risk officer asks for extra cuts before signing off.

exceptions.name: Limit breach escalated
exceptions.description: A concentration, partner or vintage trigger is breached and the director writes an action plan for the committee.

exceptions.name: Quarter-end board pages
exceptions.description: At quarter end the director condenses the monthly reports into board risk committee pages.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from month end to report presented at the credit and risk committee
benchmarks.population: Author estimate for a mid-size non-bank lessor

evidence.note: The report follows the lease system month-end batch and the subledger figures from the close (about 11 days in this organisation's close workflow) and must be ready before conduit and lender reports; conduits must publish pool performance within 50 days. No published cycle time for a lessor's internal risk report was found.

benchmarks.population: US equipment finance companies (ELFA MLFI-25 and SEFA respondents)

benchmarks.unit: share of portfolio with approved deferrals, 2020

benchmarks.population: Chesswood Group, Canadian and US equipment finance

evidence.note: Shows how quickly loss levels moved in the reference period.

pain_points.description: Restructure, deferral and recovery data arrive as emailed spreadsheets from operations, so the analyst waits and re-keys, and late corrections change figures after accounting has taken its extract.

evidence.note: Missing modification history is a documented MIS integrity problem; the hand-off is an author assessment.

pain_points.description: Most calculations live in large workbooks that need a peer check and break when codes or cohorts change.

evidence.note: Author assessment of spreadsheet-based reporting in the reference period.

pain_points.description: Reconciling warehouse balances to the ledger waits for accounting's close figures and differences are traced by hand.

evidence.note: Author assessment.

pain_points.description: Reviews and follow-up cuts add a week, so the committee sees the month two to three weeks after it ends.

evidence.note: Author assessment.

pain_points.description: Data quality problems such as missing industry or channel codes and unflagged restructures distort segment analysis.

evidence.note: Documented common MIS data integrity problems.

sources.title: Comptroller's Handbook: Loan Portfolio Management (April 1998, updated June 2017)
sources.publisher: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
sources.supports: Reports used to supervise a loan portfolio include risk rating reports, problem loan and watch list reports, delinquency and nonperforming reports, concentration reports, portfolio stratification, stress tests, exception reports and loss allowance analysis; reports to senior management and the board must be analytical, with history and trends, and board reports more summarised; common MIS data integrity problems include wrong industry codes, failure to report delinquency, outdated risk ratings and missing modification history.

sources.title: Comptroller's Handbook: Retail Lending (version 2.0, October 2021)
sources.publisher: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
sources.supports: Early-stage delinquencies are key credit quality signals; management should monitor delinquency and charge-off trends with vintage analysis (grouping loans by origination period) and lagged analysis (adjusting loss rate denominators for growth); concentrations should be identified and managed; reporting should consolidate data by business line, product, industry and region for monthly and quarterly monitoring, with dashboards of key measures against the approved risk appetite.

sources.title: New data reveals market insights (2021 Survey of Equipment Finance Activity)
sources.supports: 104 US equipment finance companies, 2020: receivables over 30 days past due rose 30 basis points to 2.3%, held in check by deferrals; net full-year losses 0.48% of average receivables; COVID deferrals approved on 7.4% of the portfolio and accepted on 7%.

sources.title: ELFA Monthly Leasing and Finance Index, July 2019 (press release)
sources.supports: Monthly industry index: receivables over 30 days 2.0% in July 2019 (1.70% the month before); charge-offs 0.37%; credit approvals 75.7%.

sources.title: Asset-based finance in Canada: the 2019-2020 year (Canadian Market Overview)
sources.supports: The CFLA/PayNet Canadian equipment delinquency indices track 30-day and 90-day small business delinquency by region and sector; rates rose through 2019 and in the first half of 2020 rose three times as much as in all of 2019, rivalling the 2009-10 recession; CFLA surveyed members on deferral requests in 2020.

sources.title: A primer on the Canadian asset-backed commercial paper market
sources.supports: Conduits must publish monthly information on asset pools and their performance in a Form 45-106F8 monthly disclosure report no later than 50 days after month end; overcollateralisation and excess spread absorb losses on the seller's pools.

sources.title: IFRS 16 (accounting news, October 2018)
sources.supports: IFRS 16 keeps the IAS 17 lessor model; a finance lessor recognises a receivable for the net investment in the lease; the IFRS 9 impairment requirements must be applied to the lease receivable.

sources.title: IFRS 9 Financial Instruments
sources.supports: IFRS 9 includes impairment requirements for an entity's expected credit losses on financial assets and is effective for annual periods beginning on or after 1 January 2018.

sources.title: Chesswood announces fiscal year 2021 results
sources.publisher: Chesswood Group Limited via Cision Newswire
sources.supports: A Canadian equipment finance group's net charge-offs were $31.4 million in 2020 and $2.0 million in 2021; the 2021 provision for credit losses fell $25.5 million to $0.2 million on releases from a better performing portfolio; management expected loss metrics to normalise in 2022.

sources.title: Principles for the Management of Credit Risk
sources.supports: A comprehensive credit risk management programme should cover a sound credit-granting process and an appropriate credit administration, measurement and monitoring process, among other areas.

assumptions: One case is one monthly report. Touch minutes are team hours (about 80 to 100 hours a month in total, mostly analysts). Several analyses run side by side (marked concurrent), but the simulator adds them in sequence, so its cycle time is a little longer than the elapsed time a team of four analysts would take.
All cases start from the month-end data load (maintain-data-and-reporting). Collections, restructure, recovery and large-exposure inputs arrive during the case, so their trigger share is 0.

The delinquency and loss extract goes to lease accounting before the full report is approved so that the loss allowance can be booked in the close; the produces link to account-for-leases-and-credit-losses therefore uses outcome 'any'.

The organisation file has no prudential regulator for this lessor, so controls rest on board-approved policy, the external auditor's reliance on the allowance inputs, and lenders' and conduits' reporting needs.

Staffing: about 0.8 of 4 portfolio analysts (the modelled steps plus ad hoc follow-up questions the report creates), 0.12 of the director, 0.02 of the chief credit and risk officer and 0.05 of a data developer. Loaded costs are the organisation file's (2019-2022 wage times 1.35).
Quarter-end board pages are modelled as one extra step a third of the time; the board pack itself belongs to report-to-board.
